en.title: Chris Hansen Refused Robert Pattinson's 'Primetime' Screening Over Rights Dispute
en.summary: Chris Hansen claims he was denied a private screening of A24's upcoming film 'Primetime' starring Robert Pattinson. The former 'To Catch a Predator' host stated that studio lawyers asked him to sign away his rights, leading to his departure without seeing the film.
en.body:
## The Screening Snag

Chris Hansen, best known for hosting the controversial series 'To Catch a Predator,' has revealed a peculiar reason for not attending a private screening of A24's forthcoming film, **Primetime**. The movie, which reportedly stars **Robert Pattinson** as Hansen, was the subject of a planned viewing at the studio's offices. However, Hansen claims he left without seeing a single frame due to a disagreement over legal rights. According to Hansen, the lawyers representing A24 presented him with documents he found unacceptable.

> “The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image and brand essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie,” Hansen stated. He elaborated that he could not agree to such terms, which ultimately resulted in him being unable to view the film he had traveled to see.

## Rights, Wrongs, and Rebuttals

The situation took a turn as sources close to the matter, including reports from Deadline, clarified that Hansen was not asked to sign an NDA in the traditional sense, but rather a release form that would impact his rights. A24 has reportedly denied Hansen's claims regarding the nature of the request. This incident raises questions about the standard procedures for screenings involving individuals whose life stories are being adapted for the screen and the fine line between protecting a studio's interests and respecting an individual's rights.

## Fan Reaction and Future Implications

News of this screening dispute has, understandably, sparked discussion among fans of both Chris Hansen's past work and the burgeoning film **Primetime**. Many are eager to see how **Robert Pattinson** will portray the polarizing figure, and this behind-the-scenes drama only adds another layer of intrigue. The community is divided, with some defending Hansen's stance on protecting his image and legal standing, while others question whether he was being overly cautious or perhaps misunderstanding standard studio protocols for such private viewings. The outcome of this disagreement could set a precedent for how similar situations are handled in the future, particularly for high-profile biographical projects.

## What's Next

Details regarding the official release date and further marketing for **Primetime** have not yet been announced by A24. However, this public disagreement ensures that the film is already generating significant buzz, even before its debut.
